The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 458 459 ```ts 460 // Before 461 revalidateTag('posts') 462 463 // After 464 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 465 ``` 466 467 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 468 469 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 470 'use server' 471 472 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 473 474 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 475 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 476 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 481 'use server' 482 483 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 484 485 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 486 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 487 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 488 } 489 ``` 490 491 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 725 726 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 760 761 If you need to support 16px images: 762 763 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 764 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 765 766 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 767 images: { 768 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 769 }, 770 } 771 772 export default nextConfig 773 ``` 774 775 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 776 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 777 const nextConfig = { 778 images: { 779 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 780 }, 781 } 782 783 module.exports = nextConfig 784 ``` 785 786 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 787 788 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 789 790 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 791 792 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 793 794 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 795 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 796 797 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 798 images: { 799 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 800 }, 801 } 802 803 export default nextConfig 804 ``` 805 806 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 807 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 808 const nextConfig = { 809 images: { 810 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 811 }, 812 } 813 814 module.exports = nextConfig 815 ``` 816 817 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. Use `next/image` instead: 882 883 ```tsx 884 // Before 885 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 886 887 // After 888 import Image from 'next/image' 889 ``` 890 891 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 892 893 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 894 895 ```js filename="next.config.js" 896 // image.domains is deprecated 897 module.exports = { 898 images: { 899 domains: ['example.com'], 900 }, 901 } 902 ``` 903 904 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 905 906 ```js filename="next.config.js" 907 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 908 module.exports = { 909 images: { 910 remotePatterns: [ 911 { 912 protocol: 'https', 913 hostname: 'example.com', 914 }, 915 ], 916 }, 917 } 918 ``` 919 920 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 921 922 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1098 1099 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1100 1101 ```bash package="pnpm" 1102 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1103 ``` 1104 1105 ```bash package="npm" 1106 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1107 ``` 1108 1109 ```bash package="yarn" 1110 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1111 ``` 1112 1113 ```bash package="bun" 1114 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1115 ``` 1116 1117 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1118 1119 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1120 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1121 const nextConfig = { 1122 // No longer supported 1123 // eslint: {}, 1124 } 1125 1126 export default nextConfig 1127 ``` 1128 1129 ### Runtime Configuration 1130 1131 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1132 1133 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1134 1135 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1136 module.exports = { 1137 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1138 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1139 }, 1140 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1141 apiUrl: '/api', 1142 }, 1143 } 1144 ``` 1145 1146 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1147 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1148 1149 export default function Page() { 1150 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1151 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1152 } 1153 ``` 1154 1155 **After (Next.js 16):** 1156 1157 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1158 1159 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1160 async function fetchData() { 1161 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1162 // Use for server-side operations only 1163 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1164 } 1165 1166 export default async function Page() { 1167 const data = await fetchData() 1168 return
{/* render data */}
1169 } 1170 ``` 1171 1172 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1173 1174 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1175 1176 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1177 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1178 ``` 1179 1180 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1181 'use client' 1182 1183 export default function ClientComponent() { 1184 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1185 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1186 } 1187 ``` 1188 1189 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1190 1191 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1192 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1193 1194 export default async function Page() { 1195 await connection() 1196 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1197 return

{config}

1198 } 1199 ``` 1200 1201 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1202 1203 ### `devIndicators` Options 1204 1205 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1206 1207 - `appIsrStatus` 1208 - `buildActivity` 1209 - `buildActivityPosition` 1210 1211 The indicator itself remains available. 1212 1213 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1214 1215 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are deprecated. Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 112 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 113 114 ## Turbopack by default 115 116 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. The migration is complete and verified (clean `tsc` + successful `next build`). Here's what I did.

## Summary

I migrated the entire Pages Router app to the App Router, deleted `pages/` entirely, and used the correct **Next.js 16** App Router APIs (I read the bundled docs first, since this canary has breaking changes vs. older Next).

### File mapping

| Pages Router (deleted) | App Router (new) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/_app.js` + `pages/_document.js` | `app/layout.tsx` | Single root layout with `<html>`/`<body>`, the `AppProvider`, header/nav/footer chrome, and `metadata` |
| `pages/index.js` (`getServerSideProps`) | `app/page.tsx` | Server Component; `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` + `await headers()` for the user-agent |
| `pages/blog/index.js` (`getStaticProps`, `revalidate: 60`) | `app/blog/page.tsx` | `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` |
| `pages/blog/[id].js` (`getStaticPaths` + `getStaticProps`) | `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` | `generateStaticParams` + `dynamicParams` (replaces `fallback: 'blocking'`); `notFound()` replaces `{ notFound: true }`; `generateMetadata` for dynamic head tags |
| `router.isFallback` loading state | `app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx` | |
| `pages/404.js` | `app/not-found.tsx` | |
| `pages/_error.js` (`getInitialProps`) | `app/error.tsx` | Client error boundary using the documented `unstable_retry` prop for this version |
| `pages/api/posts/index.js` | `app/api/posts/route.ts` | Per-method `GET`/`POST` exports; `await request.json()`; auto-405 |
| `pages/api/posts/[id].js` | `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` | `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE`; **`params` is now a `Promise`** (awaited) |

### Key breaking-change APIs applied
- **`params`/`searchParams` are Promises** in pages and route handlers — awaited everywhere.
- **`next/head` → Metadata API** (`export const metadata` / `generateMetadata`).
- **`useRouter` from `next/router` → `next/navigation`** — extracted into small `'use client'` components (`NavButton`, `BackButton`) so the pages stay Server Components.
- **`getStaticPaths` → `generateStaticParams`**, `fallback: 'blocking'` → `dynamicParams`.
- **API Routes → Route Handlers** with Web `Request`/`Response`.
- Fonts moved from the `_document` `<link>` to **`next/font/google`** (the doc explicitly notes inlined font CSS doesn't work in `app`), wired through a `--font-inter` CSS variable in `globals.css`.

### Types added
`.tsx`/`.ts` throughout, a shared `types.ts` (`Post`, `Comment`), typed context value in `AppProvider`, typed route-handler bodies/params, and typed `Metadata`/props. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

### Note
`package.json` and `package-lock.json` already had pre-existing changes from environment setup (not mine); I left them as-is. I added `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `*.tsbuildinfo` to `.gitignore` to keep generated files out of the repo.

shellCommands.command: ls -la && echo "---PACKAGE---" && cat package.json && echo "---NEXT VERSION---" && cat node_modules/next/package.json | grep '"version"'
find pages -type f 2>/dev/null | sort && echo "---SRC---" && find src -type f 2>/dev/null | sort && echo "---APP---" && find app -type f 2>/dev/null | sort

for f in pages/404.js pages/_app.js pages/_document.js pages/_error.js pages/index.js pages/blog/index.js pages/blog/\[id\].js pages/api/posts/index.js pages/api/posts/\[id\].js components/* styles/* next.config.ts tsconfig.json; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; echo; done
ls node_modules/next/dist/docs/ 2>/dev/null && echo "---NESTED---" && find node_modules/next/dist/docs/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -100

cd node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference; echo "===== page.md ====="; sed -n '1,120p' 03-file-conventions/page.md; echo "===== route.md ====="; sed -n '1,160p' 03-file-conventions/route.md

cd node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference; echo "===== generate-metadata (head) ====="; sed -n '1,90p' 04-functions/generate-metadata.md; echo "===== not-found.md ====="; sed -n '1,80p' 03-file-conventions/not-found.md

cd node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference; echo "===== error.md ====="; sed -n '1,90p' 03-file-conventions/error.md; echo "===== generate-static-params (head) ====="; sed -n '1,70p' 04-functions/generate-static-params.md
cd /workspace && rm -rf pages components/AppProvider.js && echo "Removed. Remaining tree:" && find app components styles types.ts -type f | sort
timeout 240 npx next build 2>&1 | tail -45; echo "EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
